Paracetamol.uses: Temporary relief of certain mild pain and fever.
Paracetamol.age: Age-specific use depends on the exact product and strength. Follow the product label.
Paracetamol.precautions: Do not exceed the labeled amount. Check combination cold/flu medicines for duplicate paracetamol.
Paracetamol.sideEffects: Usually tolerated when used correctly. Overdose can cause serious liver injury.
Paracetamol.interactions: Some medicines and combination products may contain the same active ingredient.
Paracetamol.status: Commonly available OTC in many markets.
Paracetamol.warning: Do not use more than directed.

Ibuprofen.purpose: NSAID pain reliever and fever reducer
Ibuprofen.uses: Temporary relief of certain pain, inflammation and fever.
Ibuprofen.age: Age restrictions vary by product. Follow the exact label.
Ibuprofen.precautions: People with certain stomach, kidney, heart or other conditions may need professional advice.
Ibuprofen.sideEffects: May cause stomach upset and other adverse effects.
Ibuprofen.interactions: Can interact with certain blood thinners and other NSAIDs.
Ibuprofen.food: Follow the product label; some people take it with food to reduce stomach upset.
Ibuprofen.status: OTC in many markets, but availability varies.
Ibuprofen.warning: Do not combine with another NSAID unless advised.

Dolo 650.uses: Temporary relief of fever and mild to moderate pain such as headache, body aches, muscle pain and toothache.
Dolo 650.dose: 650 mg per tablet. Do not use this entry as a personalized dosing calculator. Follow the exact package label or advice from a doctor/pharmacist; age, weight, liver health and other medicines can affect safe use.
Dolo 650.age: Generally intended for adults and adolescents when appropriate. Dose for children should be based on age/weight and medical guidance.
Dolo 650.precautions: Use caution in people with liver disease, heavy alcohol use, malnutrition, or those taking other medicines containing paracetamol. Follow the recommended dose.
Dolo 650.sideEffects: Usually well tolerated when used correctly. Possible side effects include nausea, stomach discomfort or allergic reactions. Serious liver damage can occur with overdose.
Dolo 650.interactions: May interact with medicines such as warfarin and other medicines containing paracetamol. Avoid taking multiple paracetamol-containing products together.
Dolo 650.food: Can be taken with or without food.
Dolo 650.status: OTC medicine in India, subject to applicable local regulations.
Dolo 650.warning: Do not exceed the recommended daily amount. Do not combine Dolo 650 with other medicines containing paracetamol unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice if fever is persistent, severe, or accompanied by concerning symptoms.

Cetirizine.uses: Relief of certain allergy symptoms such as sneezing, itching and runny nose.
Cetirizine.precautions: May cause drowsiness in some people.
Cetirizine.sideEffects: Drowsiness, tiredness or dry mouth may occur.
Cetirizine.interactions: Other medicines that cause drowsiness may increase this effect.
Cetirizine.food: Usually can be taken with or without food; follow the label.
Cetirizine.warning: Do not drive or operate machinery if it makes you drowsy.

Loratadine.age: Follow the exact product's age directions.
Loratadine.sideEffects: Headache, tiredness or dry mouth may occur.
Loratadine.interactions: Tell a pharmacist or doctor about other medicines.
Loratadine.warning: Seek urgent care for severe allergic reactions.

Omeprazole.uses: Reduces stomach acid and is used for certain acid-related conditions.
Omeprazole.age: Age and duration depend on the exact product and condition.
Omeprazole.precautions: Persistent or recurrent symptoms should be medically evaluated.
Omeprazole.sideEffects: Headache, nausea or abdominal symptoms can occur.
Omeprazole.interactions: Can interact with some prescription and non-prescription medicines.
Omeprazole.food: Product directions may specify timing in relation to meals.
Omeprazole.status: OTC or prescription depending on product and country.
Omeprazole.warning: Do not use longer than the product label recommends without medical advice.

Antacid.uses: Temporary relief of heartburn and acid indigestion.
Antacid.sideEffects: Some products may cause constipation or diarrhea.
Antacid.interactions: Some antacids can affect absorption of other medicines.
Antacid.warning: Persistent or severe chest or abdominal symptoms require medical evaluation.

ORS.uses: Helps replace fluids and electrolytes lost through diarrhea or vomiting.
ORS.age: Use an age-appropriate product and follow preparation instructions.
ORS.precautions: Prepare exactly according to the package directions.
ORS.sideEffects: Incorrect preparation can cause inappropriate electrolyte intake.
ORS.interactions: Medical conditions affecting fluid balance may require professional advice.
ORS.food: Used as a fluid replacement rather than a conventional tablet medicine.
ORS.warning: Severe dehydration or inability to drink requires urgent medical care.

Dextromethorphan.precautions: Do not exceed labeled directions. Check combination cough/cold products.
Dextromethorphan.sideEffects: Drowsiness, dizziness or nausea can occur.
Dextromethorphan.interactions: Can interact with some medicines, including certain serotonergic medicines.
Dextromethorphan.warning: Persistent or worsening cough requires medical evaluation.

Saline Nasal Spray.uses: Helps moisturize the nose and loosen nasal mucus.
Saline Nasal Spray.warning: Persistent severe nasal symptoms require evaluation.

Clotrimazole.uses: Used for certain superficial fungal skin infections.
Clotrimazole.age: Age suitability depends on the product and treatment area.
Clotrimazole.precautions: For external use according to product instructions.
Clotrimazole.sideEffects: Local irritation or redness may occur.
Clotrimazole.interactions: Ask a pharmacist if using other topical medicines on the same area.
Clotrimazole.warning: Persistent or worsening rash should be professionally evaluated.

Hydrocortisone.uses: May reduce inflammation and itching in certain skin conditions.
Hydrocortisone.age: Use in children and on sensitive areas according to professional/product guidance.
Hydrocortisone.precautions: Do not use on an undiagnosed infection without appropriate advice.
Hydrocortisone.sideEffects: Skin irritation can occur; prolonged inappropriate use can thin skin.
Hydrocortisone.interactions: Tell a healthcare professional about other topical medicines.
Hydrocortisone.status: OTC or prescription depending on strength and country.
Hydrocortisone.warning: Worsening redness, pain, pus or fever may indicate infection.

Benzoyl Peroxide.precautions: Can cause dryness and irritation. Avoid eyes.
Benzoyl Peroxide.interactions: Other irritating skin products can increase irritation.
Benzoyl Peroxide.warning: Stop and seek advice for severe irritation or allergic reaction.

Loperamide.uses: May reduce diarrhea in appropriate situations.
Loperamide.precautions: Do not use for certain bloody or infectious diarrhea without medical advice.
Loperamide.sideEffects: Constipation, abdominal discomfort or nausea may occur.
Loperamide.interactions: Ask a pharmacist about other medicines.
Loperamide.warning: Blood in stool, high fever or severe abdominal pain requires medical evaluation.

Salbutamol Inhaler.uses: Relieves wheezing and shortness of breath by relaxing airway muscles.
Salbutamol Inhaler.age: Age-specific use depends on the exact product. Follow the product label.
Salbutamol Inhaler.precautions: Often prescription-only; asthma should be diagnosed and monitored by a doctor.
Salbutamol Inhaler.sideEffects: Tremor, rapid heartbeat or nervousness may occur.
Salbutamol Inhaler.interactions: Certain heart medicines and other bronchodilators may interact.
Salbutamol Inhaler.status: Prescription or pharmacist-supervised in many markets.
Salbutamol Inhaler.warning: Seek urgent care if breathing difficulty is severe or not relieved.

Simethicone.uses: Relieves bloating and discomfort caused by excess gas.
Simethicone.food: Usually taken after meals; follow the label.
Simethicone.warning: Persistent bloating or pain should be medically evaluated.

Psyllium Husk (Isabgol).uses: Helps relieve constipation and supports regular bowel movements.
Psyllium Husk (Isabgol).precautions: Take with adequate water to avoid choking or blockage.
Psyllium Husk (Isabgol).sideEffects: Bloating or gas, especially when starting use.
Psyllium Husk (Isabgol).interactions: May affect absorption of some medicines if taken at the same time.
Psyllium Husk (Isabgol).food: Usually mixed with water or milk; follow the label.
Psyllium Husk (Isabgol).warning: Persistent constipation should be medically evaluated.

Bisacodyl.uses: Provides short-term relief of occasional constipation.
Bisacodyl.precautions: Not intended for long-term regular use.
Bisacodyl.interactions: Ask a pharmacist about use with other medicines.
Bisacodyl.warning: Persistent or severe constipation requires medical evaluation.

Domperidone.uses: Used for relief of nausea and vomiting.
Domperidone.age: Age restrictions apply; follow product label or medical advice.
Domperidone.precautions: May be prescription-only in some countries due to heart-rhythm concerns.
Domperidone.sideEffects: Rarely, heart rhythm changes; dry mouth or headache may occur.
Domperidone.interactions: Can interact with certain heart and other medicines.
Domperidone.food: Usually taken before meals; follow the label.
Domperidone.status: OTC or prescription depending on country.
Domperidone.warning: Persistent vomiting or signs of dehydration require medical care.

Ketoconazole Shampoo.uses: Helps reduce flaking and itching associated with dandruff.
Ketoconazole Shampoo.precautions: For external scalp use only; avoid contact with eyes.
Ketoconazole Shampoo.sideEffects: Scalp irritation or dryness may occur.
Ketoconazole Shampoo.interactions: Few known interactions with topical use.
Ketoconazole Shampoo.warning: Persistent or worsening scalp irritation should be evaluated.

Lubricating Eye Drops.uses: Soothes eye irritation, dryness and discomfort.
Lubricating Eye Drops.age: Generally suitable for most ages; follow the label.
Lubricating Eye Drops.precautions: Does not treat infection; bacterial conjunctivitis needs prescription drops.
Lubricating Eye Drops.sideEffects: Mild, temporary blurring or stinging may occur.
Lubricating Eye Drops.warning: Eye pain, vision change or thick discharge needs prompt medical evaluation.

Iron Supplement.uses: Used to address iron-deficiency related low blood counts.
Iron Supplement.age: Follow the product-specific label or medical advice.
Iron Supplement.precautions: Best confirmed by a doctor with a blood test before long-term use.
Iron Supplement.sideEffects: Constipation, dark stools or stomach upset may occur.
Iron Supplement.interactions: Can reduce absorption of some other medicines if taken together.
Iron Supplement.food: Often taken with food to reduce stomach upset; follow the label.
Iron Supplement.warning: Keep out of reach of children; iron overdose can be dangerous.

Folic Acid.uses: Supports red blood cell production, often alongside iron for anemia.
Folic Acid.age: Follow the product-specific label or medical advice.
Folic Acid.precautions: Usually well tolerated at standard doses.
Folic Acid.interactions: Ask a pharmacist about use with certain other medicines.
Folic Acid.food: Can usually be taken with or without food.
Folic Acid.warning: Underlying cause of anemia should be medically evaluated.

Vitamin D3 Supplement.uses: Addresses vitamin D deficiency and supports bone health.
Vitamin D3 Supplement.age: Follow the product-specific label or medical advice.
Vitamin D3 Supplement.precautions: Very high doses over time can cause toxicity.
Vitamin D3 Supplement.interactions: Ask a pharmacist about use with certain other medicines.
Vitamin D3 Supplement.food: Often taken with a meal for better absorption.
Vitamin D3 Supplement.warning: Confirm deficiency and dosing with a healthcare professional.

Vitamin B12 Supplement.uses: Addresses vitamin B12 deficiency, supporting nerve and blood health.
Vitamin B12 Supplement.age: Follow the product-specific label or medical advice.
Vitamin B12 Supplement.precautions: Severe deficiency may need injections under medical supervision.
Vitamin B12 Supplement.interactions: Ask a pharmacist about use with certain other medicines.
Vitamin B12 Supplement.food: Can usually be taken with or without food.
Vitamin B12 Supplement.warning: Confirm deficiency and dosing with a healthcare professional.

Multivitamin.uses: May help support general energy and nutritional levels.
Multivitamin.precautions: Not a substitute for evaluating the underlying cause of persistent fatigue.
Multivitamin.interactions: Ask a pharmacist about use with certain other medicines.
Multivitamin.warning: Persistent fatigue should be medically evaluated.

Melatonin.uses: May help with occasional difficulty falling asleep.
Melatonin.age: Availability and age restrictions vary by country; follow the label.
Melatonin.precautions: Not regulated as OTC in all countries; check local status.
Melatonin.sideEffects: Drowsiness, headache or dizziness may occur.
Melatonin.interactions: May interact with certain other medicines; ask a pharmacist.
Melatonin.status: OTC in some markets, prescription-only in others.
Melatonin.warning: Persistent insomnia should be medically evaluated.

Dimenhydrinate.uses: Helps prevent and relieve motion sickness symptoms.
Dimenhydrinate.age: Age restrictions vary by product; follow the label.
Dimenhydrinate.precautions: May cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery.
Dimenhydrinate.sideEffects: Drowsiness, dry mouth or blurred vision may occur.
Dimenhydrinate.interactions: Other sedating medicines may increase drowsiness.
Dimenhydrinate.food: Usually taken before travel; follow the label.
Dimenhydrinate.warning: Consult a doctor before use in young children.

Diclofenac Gel.uses: Local relief of muscle, joint and sprain-related pain and swelling.
Diclofenac Gel.age: Usually for adults and older adolescents; follow the exact product label.
Diclofenac Gel.precautions: Apply only to intact skin. Avoid eyes, mouth and broken skin. Wash hands after use. Use caution if you have asthma triggered by NSAIDs, or stomach, kidney or heart problems.
Diclofenac Gel.sideEffects: Local skin redness, itching or irritation. Rarely, allergic reactions.
Diclofenac Gel.interactions: Avoid using together with oral NSAIDs unless advised. Tell a professional if you take blood thinners.
Diclofenac Gel.status: OTC in many markets; strength and availability vary.
Diclofenac Gel.warning: Do not apply under tight bandages or heat pads unless the label allows.

Pain Relief Balm / Spray.ingredient: Counter-irritants such as menthol, methyl salicylate or camphor
Pain Relief Balm / Spray.purpose: Topical muscle and joint pain relief
Pain Relief Balm / Spray.uses: Temporary warming or cooling relief for minor muscle aches, stiffness and sprains.
Pain Relief Balm / Spray.age: Not for young children; check the label for the minimum age.
Pain Relief Balm / Spray.precautions: Use only on intact skin. Avoid eyes, mucous membranes and open wounds. Do not use with heating pads. Methyl salicylate products can be risky for people allergic to aspirin or on blood thinners.
Pain Relief Balm / Spray.interactions: Methyl salicylate may add to the effect of blood thinners if used over large areas.
Pain Relief Balm / Spray.warning: Keep out of reach of children; swallowing can be toxic.

Aspirin.purpose: NSAID pain reliever and fever reducer
Aspirin.uses: Temporary relief of mild to moderate pain such as headache.
Aspirin.age: Not generally given to children or teenagers under 16 because of the risk of Reye's syndrome. Follow the product label.
Aspirin.precautions: Avoid in people with stomach ulcers, bleeding disorders, asthma triggered by NSAIDs, or in late pregnancy unless a doctor advises. Do not start daily low-dose use without medical advice.
Aspirin.sideEffects: Stomach irritation or bleeding, heartburn, easy bruising, allergic reactions.
Aspirin.interactions: Interacts with blood thinners, other NSAIDs, some diabetes and blood pressure medicines.
Aspirin.food: Taking with food may reduce stomach upset.
Aspirin.status: OTC in many markets; availability varies.
Aspirin.warning: Do not combine with another NSAID unless advised. Do not give to children or teens for fever.

Famotidine.uses: Relief and prevention of heartburn and acid indigestion.
Famotidine.age: Check label; not for young children without medical advice.
Famotidine.precautions: People with kidney problems may need professional advice. Seek care if heartburn is frequent, severe or comes with trouble swallowing, weight loss or black stools.
Famotidine.interactions: May affect absorption of some medicines (e.g., certain antifungals and HIV medicines).
Famotidine.food: Can be taken with or without food; follow the label.
Famotidine.status: OTC in some markets; prescription-only in others.

Levocetirizine.uses: Relief of sneezing, runny nose, itching and watery eyes from allergies; itchy skin.
Levocetirizine.age: Age-specific forms exist; follow the label or a doctor's advice.
Levocetirizine.precautions: May cause drowsiness in some people. Use caution with kidney problems. Avoid alcohol and driving if drowsy.
Levocetirizine.interactions: Additive sedation with alcohol or sedative medicines.
Levocetirizine.food: Can be taken with or without food.
Levocetirizine.status: Availability varies by country; commonly sold OTC in India.
Levocetirizine.warning: Do not combine with other antihistamines unless advised.

Fexofenadine.uses: Relief of sneezing, runny nose, itchy or watery eyes and itching from allergies.
Fexofenadine.age: Age-specific strengths exist; follow the label.
Fexofenadine.sideEffects: Headache, nausea, dizziness; drowsiness is uncommon.
Fexofenadine.interactions: Antacids with aluminium/magnesium and fruit juices (grapefruit, orange, apple) can reduce absorption.
Fexofenadine.food: Take with water; avoid fruit juice around the dose.
Fexofenadine.status: OTC in many markets; availability varies.
Fexofenadine.warning: Do not take with fruit juice.

Chlorpheniramine.form: Tablet / Syrup (often in combination cold products)
Chlorpheniramine.uses: Relief of sneezing, runny nose and itching from colds and allergies.
Chlorpheniramine.age: Not suitable for very young children; follow the label.
Chlorpheniramine.precautions: Causes drowsiness. Use caution with glaucoma, enlarged prostate, urinary retention, or if driving. Check combination products for duplicate ingredients.
Chlorpheniramine.sideEffects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, blurred vision, urinary difficulty.
Chlorpheniramine.interactions: Additive sedation with alcohol, sleeping pills or other antihistamines.
Chlorpheniramine.food: Can be taken with or without food.
Chlorpheniramine.status: Commonly OTC, often as part of combination cold medicines.
Chlorpheniramine.warning: Do not drive or operate machinery if drowsy.

Xylometazoline Nasal Spray.uses: Short-term relief of blocked nose from colds, sinusitis or allergies.
Xylometazoline Nasal Spray.age: Child-strength products differ; follow the label.
Xylometazoline Nasal Spray.precautions: Use only for the short period stated on the label (usually a few days). Caution with high blood pressure, heart disease, thyroid disease or glaucoma.
Xylometazoline Nasal Spray.sideEffects: Nasal dryness, stinging, sneezing. Longer use can cause rebound congestion.
Xylometazoline Nasal Spray.warning: Prolonged use can worsen congestion (rebound effect).

Guaifenesin.form: Syrup / Tablet (often in combination cough products)
Guaifenesin.uses: Relief of chest congestion with thick mucus.
Guaifenesin.age: Check the label; not suitable for young children in many products.
Guaifenesin.precautions: Drink plenty of fluids. Seek care if cough lasts more than about a week, or comes with fever, rash, persistent headache or breathlessness.
Guaifenesin.sideEffects: Nausea, vomiting, dizziness or stomach upset.
Guaifenesin.interactions: Check combination products for duplicate ingredients.
Guaifenesin.food: Take with water; follow the label.

Ambroxol.uses: Helps clear mucus in productive cough and bronchitis.
Ambroxol.age: Pediatric forms exist; follow the label or doctor's advice.
Ambroxol.precautions: Use caution with stomach ulcers or severe liver/kidney disease. Stop and seek care if skin reactions occur.
Ambroxol.sideEffects: Nausea, stomach upset, taste changes. Rare allergic or skin reactions.
Ambroxol.interactions: Usually few interactions; avoid combining with cough suppressants unless advised.
Ambroxol.status: Commonly sold OTC or on pharmacist advice in India; varies elsewhere.
Ambroxol.warning: Do not use with cough suppressants without advice.

Throat Lozenges.uses: Temporary relief of sore throat and throat irritation.
Throat Lozenges.age: Not suitable for young children (choking risk); follow the label.
Throat Lozenges.precautions: Check ingredients if you have allergies or diabetes (sugar content). Seek care if sore throat is severe, lasts over a few days or comes with high fever.
Throat Lozenges.sideEffects: Mouth irritation or numbness; rare allergic reactions.
Throat Lozenges.interactions: Avoid doubling up with other products containing the same active ingredient.
Throat Lozenges.food: Dissolve slowly; avoid eating or drinking right after if numbing.
Throat Lozenges.warning: Persistent sore throat needs medical evaluation.

Calamine Lotion.uses: Relieves itching and irritation from insect bites, heat rash, mild sunburn and minor skin rashes.
Calamine Lotion.age: Generally suitable across ages when used on skin; check the label.
Calamine Lotion.precautions: Do not apply to broken or severely blistered skin, or near the eyes. Stop if irritation worsens.
Calamine Lotion.interactions: No significant interactions when applied to skin.

Povidone-Iodine.uses: Cleaning minor cuts, scrapes and wounds to reduce infection risk.
Povidone-Iodine.age: Use with care in infants; follow the label.
Povidone-Iodine.precautions: Do not use on deep wounds, serious burns or animal bites without medical advice. Avoid with iodine allergy or thyroid disorders and avoid long or large-area use.
Povidone-Iodine.interactions: May be inactivated by some other antiseptics; can affect thyroid tests.
Povidone-Iodine.warning: For external use only; do not swallow.

Terbinafine Cream.uses: Treats athlete's foot, ringworm and jock itch.
Terbinafine Cream.precautions: Keep the area clean and dry. Complete the full course even if symptoms fade. Avoid eyes and mouth. See a doctor if no improvement or if nails/scalp are involved.
Terbinafine Cream.sideEffects: Mild itching, burning or redness at the application site.
Terbinafine Cream.interactions: No significant interactions expected with topical use.

Permethrin.age: Age restrictions vary; follow the label or doctor's advice.
Permethrin.precautions: Follow the label exactly; household contacts and bedding may also need treatment. Avoid eyes and broken skin. Itching can persist for weeks after successful treatment.
Permethrin.sideEffects: Temporary itching, burning, redness or tingling.
Permethrin.interactions: No significant interactions expected with topical use.
Permethrin.status: OTC in some markets; may need a prescription in others.
Permethrin.warning: Do not use on infants without medical advice.

Albendazole.age: Use in young children only as directed by a doctor.
Albendazole.precautions: Avoid in pregnancy unless a doctor advises. People with liver disease need medical guidance. Household hygiene and treating close contacts matter.
Albendazole.interactions: Some medicines (e.g., certain anticonvulsants, cimetidine) can change its levels.
Albendazole.food: Often taken with food (especially fatty food) to improve absorption; follow instructions.
Albendazole.status: Prescription status varies; commonly dispensed on pharmacist or doctor advice.
Albendazole.warning: Seek medical advice before use in pregnancy or for children.

Hyoscine Butylbromide.uses: Relief of abdominal cramps and spasms, including with IBS.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.age: Usually for adults and older children; follow the label.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.precautions: Avoid with glaucoma, enlarged prostate, urinary retention, myasthenia gravis or bowel obstruction. Seek care for severe or persistent abdominal pain.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.sideEffects: Dry mouth, dizziness, fast heartbeat, constipation.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.interactions: Additive effect with other anticholinergic medicines such as some antihistamines.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.food: Can be taken with or without food.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.status: OTC in some markets, prescription-only in others.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.warning: Severe abdominal pain, fever or blood in stool needs medical care.

Probiotics.ingredient: Live beneficial bacteria or yeast (e.g., Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, Saccharomyces)
Probiotics.uses: May help with some types of diarrhea and with digestive symptoms such as IBS or bloating.
Probiotics.precautions: People with weakened immunity, central lines or serious illness should consult a doctor first. Effects vary between strains and products.
Probiotics.interactions: Take apart from antibiotics unless the label says otherwise; antifungal medicines may reduce yeast-based probiotics.
Probiotics.status: Sold as supplements or food products.
Probiotics.warning: Not a substitute for fluids (ORS) in diarrhea.

Zinc Supplement.uses: Used with ORS in children's diarrhea under medical guidance, and for zinc deficiency.
Zinc Supplement.age: Pediatric dosing should follow medical guidance or label.
Zinc Supplement.precautions: Do not exceed the labeled amount; high intake can cause copper deficiency. Can cause nausea on an empty stomach.
Zinc Supplement.interactions: Can reduce absorption of some antibiotics (quinolones, tetracyclines) and iron.
Zinc Supplement.food: Taking with food may reduce stomach upset.
Zinc Supplement.warning: Do not exceed the labeled amount.

Calcium Supplement.ingredient: Calcium carbonate or citrate (often with vitamin D3)
Calcium Supplement.uses: Helps meet calcium needs when diet is not enough.
Calcium Supplement.age: Follow the label for age-appropriate products.
Calcium Supplement.precautions: Avoid excess; people with kidney stones, high blood calcium or kidney disease need medical advice.
Calcium Supplement.interactions: Can reduce absorption of some antibiotics, thyroid medicine and iron; separate by a few hours.
Calcium Supplement.food: Calcium carbonate is best with food; calcium citrate can be taken any time.
Calcium Supplement.warning: Do not exceed the labeled amount.

Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.uses: Helps reduce plaque and gum inflammation (gingivitis) and supports mouth hygiene.
Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.age: Not for young children who may swallow it; follow the label.
Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.precautions: Do not swallow. Typically for short-term use; can stain teeth or tongue. See a dentist for persistent gum problems.
Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.sideEffects: Teeth or tongue staining, temporary taste change, mouth irritation.
Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.interactions: Some toothpastes may reduce its effect; rinse mouth between brushing and mouthwash.
Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.food: Avoid eating or drinking right after use.
Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.warning: Not a replacement for brushing and dental care.

Oral Pain Relief Gel.ingredient: Choline salicylate / benzocaine / lidocaine (varies by product)
Oral Pain Relief Gel.purpose: Topical mouth ulcer and gum pain relief
Oral Pain Relief Gel.uses: Temporary relief of pain from mouth ulcers and minor gum irritation.
Oral Pain Relief Gel.age: Salicylate-containing gels are generally not for young children; follow the label.
Oral Pain Relief Gel.precautions: Apply a small amount with clean hands. See a doctor or dentist if ulcers last more than about 2–3 weeks or recur often.
Oral Pain Relief Gel.interactions: Avoid if allergic to aspirin or local anesthetics.
Oral Pain Relief Gel.food: Avoid eating or drinking right after application.
Oral Pain Relief Gel.warning: Do not use on large areas or for long periods.

Carbamide Peroxide Ear Drops.uses: Helps soften and loosen earwax buildup.
Carbamide Peroxide Ear Drops.age: Not for infants; follow the label.
Carbamide Peroxide Ear Drops.precautions: Do not use if you have ear pain, discharge, a perforated eardrum, or ear surgery history. Do not use cotton buds or sharp objects to remove wax.
Carbamide Peroxide Ear Drops.sideEffects: Mild irritation, fizzing sensation, temporary muffled hearing.
Carbamide Peroxide Ear Drops.warning: See a doctor if pain, discharge or hearing loss occurs.

Aloe Vera Gel.uses: Soothes mild sunburn and minor first-degree burns once the skin is cooled.
Aloe Vera Gel.age: Generally suitable across ages when used on skin.
Aloe Vera Gel.precautions: For mild burns, cool the area with running water first. Use pure or cosmetic-grade gel; avoid on open wounds or blistered skin. Patch-test if sensitive.
Aloe Vera Gel.interactions: No significant interactions with topical use.
Aloe Vera Gel.status: Widely available as a cosmetic/OTC product.
Aloe Vera Gel.warning: Seek medical care for large, deep, blistering or face/genital burns.

Emollient / Moisturizer.ingredient: Petrolatum, glycerin, ceramides, liquid paraffin or similar
Emollient / Moisturizer.uses: Relieves dry, flaky or itchy skin and supports eczema and psoriasis care.
Emollient / Moisturizer.age: Suitable across ages; choose fragrance-free products for sensitive skin.
Emollient / Moisturizer.precautions: Apply generously and often, ideally after bathing. Patch-test if prone to allergies. Paraffin-based products can be flammable on fabrics.
Emollient / Moisturizer.sideEffects: Occasional stinging or rash from fragrances or preservatives.
Emollient / Moisturizer.interactions: May reduce absorption of other creams if applied immediately before them.
Emollient / Moisturizer.warning: Keep away from open flames if using paraffin-based products.

Acyclovir Cream.uses: Reduces duration of cold sores (herpes labialis) when started at the first tingle.
Acyclovir Cream.precautions: Use on lips and face only; avoid eyes and inside the mouth. Wash hands after use. Contagious until healed. See a doctor if sores are frequent or severe.
Acyclovir Cream.interactions: No significant interactions with topical use.
Acyclovir Cream.status: OTC in some markets; prescription in others.
Acyclovir Cream.warning: Do not share towels or touch sores.

Salicylic Acid.uses: Helps treat acne, warts and thickened skin.
Salicylic Acid.age: Check label; avoid on infants and very large areas in children.
Salicylic Acid.precautions: Avoid broken or inflamed skin, face for wart products, and eyes. Can cause dryness and peeling. Do not use on diabetic foot ulcers or with poor circulation without medical advice.
Salicylic Acid.interactions: Avoid combining with other strong exfoliants or retinoids unless advised.
Salicylic Acid.warning: For external use only; stop if burning or severe irritation occurs.

Sunscreen.ingredient: UV filters (SPF 30 or higher, broad spectrum)
Sunscreen.uses: Helps prevent sunburn and sun damage.
Sunscreen.age: Babies under 6 months should be kept out of direct sun; follow pediatric advice.
Sunscreen.precautions: Apply generously and reapply as directed, especially after sweating or swimming. Patch-test if you have sensitive skin.
Sunscreen.sideEffects: Skin irritation or breakouts in some people.
Sunscreen.warning: Sunscreen reduces but does not eliminate risk; use shade and clothing too.

Lactulose.age: Use in children only as directed by label or doctor.
Lactulose.precautions: Can cause gas and cramps. Avoid in people with galactose intolerance; use caution with diabetes. Seek care for constipation with severe pain, vomiting or blood in stool.
Lactulose.sideEffects: Bloating, gas, abdominal cramps, loose stools.
Lactulose.interactions: Other laxatives may add to effects.
Lactulose.food: Follow the label; drink adequate fluids.
Lactulose.warning: Prolonged laxative use should be medically supervised.

Menthol Vapor Balm.uses: Gives a cooling sensation that helps with feeling of blocked nose from colds.
Menthol Vapor Balm.age: Not for infants or very young children (check label, often not under 2–3 years).
Menthol Vapor Balm.precautions: Apply externally to chest/neck as directed; do not apply to broken skin, nostrils or face of young children. Avoid contact with eyes. Do not heat or microwave.
Menthol Vapor Balm.sideEffects: Skin irritation; vapors may irritate airways, especially in asthma.
Menthol Vapor Balm.interactions: No significant interactions with external use.
Menthol Vapor Balm.warning: Camphor is toxic if swallowed; keep away from children.

Naproxen.uses: Temporary relief of headache, muscle and joint pain, menstrual cramps and inflammation.
Naproxen.age: Age limits vary by product; generally adults and older adolescents. Follow the label.
Naproxen.precautions: Use caution with stomach ulcers, kidney, heart or liver problems, asthma triggered by NSAIDs, and in pregnancy.
Naproxen.sideEffects: Stomach upset, heartburn, dizziness; rarely stomach bleeding or kidney effects.
Naproxen.interactions: Can interact with blood thinners, other NSAIDs, aspirin, some blood pressure medicines and lithium.
Naproxen.food: Take with food or milk to reduce stomach upset.
Naproxen.status: OTC in some markets, prescription-only in others.
Naproxen.warning: Do not combine with other NSAIDs such as ibuprofen, diclofenac or aspirin.

Mefenamic Acid.purpose: NSAID for pain, especially period pain
Mefenamic Acid.uses: Short-term relief of menstrual cramps and mild to moderate pain.
Mefenamic Acid.age: Age-specific use depends on the product. Follow the label or medical advice.
Mefenamic Acid.precautions: Avoid in people with stomach ulcers, kidney disease, or NSAID-triggered asthma. Use for the shortest time needed.
Mefenamic Acid.sideEffects: Nausea, stomach pain, diarrhea, dizziness; rarely stomach bleeding or kidney problems.
Mefenamic Acid.interactions: Can interact with blood thinners, other NSAIDs and some blood pressure medicines.
Mefenamic Acid.food: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
Mefenamic Acid.status: Availability varies; often pharmacy-sold or prescription depending on the country.
Mefenamic Acid.warning: Stop and seek care if you develop severe diarrhea, rash or black stools.

Ibuprofen Gel.uses: Relief of localized muscle, joint and sprain pain.
Ibuprofen Gel.age: Age limits vary; follow the label.
Ibuprofen Gel.precautions: Apply only to intact skin; avoid eyes, mouth and broken skin. Wash hands after use. Avoid with NSAID-triggered asthma.
Ibuprofen Gel.sideEffects: Local skin redness, itching or irritation.
Ibuprofen Gel.interactions: Systemic absorption is low, but caution with oral NSAIDs and blood thinners.
Ibuprofen Gel.warning: Do not cover with tight bandages or heat pads unless the label allows.

Capsaicin Cream.uses: Temporary relief of minor muscle and joint aches.
Capsaicin Cream.age: Generally for adults and older children; follow the label.
Capsaicin Cream.precautions: Do not apply to broken skin or near eyes. Wash hands thoroughly after use. Avoid heat or hot showers on treated area.
Capsaicin Cream.sideEffects: Burning, warmth or redness at the application site, especially at first.
Capsaicin Cream.interactions: No significant common interactions with topical use.
Capsaicin Cream.warning: Do not use with heating pads or tight wraps.

Lidocaine Gel / Ointment.uses: Temporary relief of pain and itching from minor burns, insect bites, hemorrhoids, minor skin irritation and sore areas.
Lidocaine Gel / Ointment.age: Age limits are strict for some forms; follow the label.
Lidocaine Gel / Ointment.precautions: Do not apply over large areas, broken or severely injured skin, or for long periods. Avoid contact with eyes.
Lidocaine Gel / Ointment.sideEffects: Local irritation, redness; allergic reactions are possible.
Lidocaine Gel / Ointment.interactions: Can add to the effect of other local anesthetics or certain heart rhythm medicines if used heavily.
Lidocaine Gel / Ointment.status: OTC in lower strengths; stronger forms may need a prescription.
Lidocaine Gel / Ointment.warning: Do not use on large areas or with heat; seek advice for children.

Glucosamine Supplement.uses: Used by some people to support joint comfort in mild osteoarthritis.
Glucosamine Supplement.age: Generally for adults. Follow the label.
Glucosamine Supplement.precautions: Avoid in shellfish allergy unless the product is shellfish-free. Use caution with diabetes, asthma, or bleeding disorders.
Glucosamine Supplement.interactions: May interact with warfarin and affect blood sugar in some people.
Glucosamine Supplement.warning: Benefit is modest and not guaranteed; not a substitute for medical care.

Pseudoephedrine.uses: Temporary relief of nasal and sinus congestion.
Pseudoephedrine.age: Not for young children; age limits vary. Follow the label.
Pseudoephedrine.precautions: Avoid in uncontrolled high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, enlarged prostate, overactive thyroid. May cause sleeplessness if taken late.
Pseudoephedrine.sideEffects: Fast heartbeat, nervousness, trouble sleeping, increased blood pressure.
Pseudoephedrine.interactions: Do not use with MAO inhibitors; caution with other stimulants and blood pressure medicines.
Pseudoephedrine.food: Can be taken with or without food.
Pseudoephedrine.status: Sold behind the counter or restricted in many markets; may be Rx-only.
Pseudoephedrine.warning: Do not combine with other decongestant products.

Oxymetazoline Nasal Spray.uses: Short-term relief of blocked nose from colds, allergies and sinus congestion.
Oxymetazoline Nasal Spray.age: Age limits vary; follow the label.
Oxymetazoline Nasal Spray.precautions: Use only for a few days; prolonged use can cause rebound congestion. Caution with high blood pressure or heart disease.
Oxymetazoline Nasal Spray.sideEffects: Nasal dryness, burning, sneezing, rebound congestion.
Oxymetazoline Nasal Spray.interactions: Avoid with MAO inhibitors; caution with other decongestants.
Oxymetazoline Nasal Spray.warning: Do not use for more than about 3 days unless advised.

Fluticasone Nasal Spray.uses: Prevention and relief of sneezing, itching and congestion from allergic rhinitis.
Fluticasone Nasal Spray.age: Age limits vary by product. Follow the label.
Fluticasone Nasal Spray.precautions: Takes several days for full effect. Avoid in untreated nasal infections; use properly aimed spray to reduce nosebleeds.
Fluticasone Nasal Spray.sideEffects: Nasal dryness, nosebleeds, headache, throat irritation.
Fluticasone Nasal Spray.interactions: Some medicines (e.g., ritonavir, ketoconazole) can raise levels.
Fluticasone Nasal Spray.status: OTC in some markets, prescription-only in others.
Fluticasone Nasal Spray.warning: Use regularly as directed; not for instant relief.

Desloratadine.uses: Relief of sneezing, runny nose, itching and hives from allergies.
Desloratadine.age: Age-specific by product. Follow the label.
Desloratadine.precautions: Use caution in kidney or liver problems and pregnancy.
Desloratadine.interactions: Few interactions; avoid with other antihistamines unless advised.
Desloratadine.status: OTC or prescription depending on country.
Desloratadine.warning: Do not combine with other antihistamines.

Diphenhydramine.uses: Relief of allergy symptoms, itching, motion sickness and short-term sleep difficulty.
Diphenhydramine.age: Not suitable for young children in oral forms; avoid in older adults. Follow the label.
Diphenhydramine.precautions: Causes drowsiness. Avoid with glaucoma, enlarged prostate, breathing problems, or when driving. Avoid alcohol.
Diphenhydramine.sideEffects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, confusion in older adults.
Diphenhydramine.interactions: Adds to the sedation of alcohol, sleep aids and other antihistamines.
Diphenhydramine.warning: Do not use with other products containing diphenhydramine.

Phenylephrine.uses: Temporary relief of stuffy nose in combination cold products.
Phenylephrine.age: Age limits vary. Follow the label.
Phenylephrine.precautions: Caution with high blood pressure, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes.
Phenylephrine.interactions: Avoid with MAO inhibitors; check other cold products for duplicates.
Phenylephrine.warning: Oral effectiveness is limited; do not stack decongestants.

Bromhexine.uses: Thinning and loosening mucus in productive cough.
Bromhexine.age: Age and strength depend on the product. Follow the label.
Bromhexine.precautions: Use caution with stomach ulcers; rare skin reactions.
Bromhexine.interactions: Combination with cough suppressants is not advisable.
Bromhexine.status: OTC in some markets, prescription in others.
Bromhexine.warning: Avoid combining with cough suppressants unless a doctor advises.

Acetylcysteine.uses: Loosening thick mucus in chest congestion and productive cough.
Acetylcysteine.age: Age and strength depend on the product. Follow the label.
Acetylcysteine.precautions: Use caution with asthma and stomach ulcers.
Acetylcysteine.interactions: Can reduce the effect of some antibiotics if taken at the same time.
Acetylcysteine.status: OTC in some markets, prescription in others.
Acetylcysteine.warning: Do not combine with cough suppressants unless advised.

Honey-Based Cough Syrup.uses: Soothing relief of throat irritation and minor cough.
Honey-Based Cough Syrup.age: Not for infants under 1 year because of botulism risk.
Honey-Based Cough Syrup.precautions: Contains sugar; use caution in diabetes.
Honey-Based Cough Syrup.warning: Do not give to infants under 1 year.

Benzydamine.uses: Relief of sore throat, mouth ulcers and gum pain.
Benzydamine.age: Age limits vary; follow the label.
Benzydamine.precautions: Use caution with NSAID-triggered asthma; do not swallow mouthwash.
Benzydamine.interactions: No significant interactions with topical use.
Benzydamine.food: Use after food for best contact time.
Benzydamine.warning: Do not use for more than a week without advice.

Pantoprazole.uses: Relief of frequent heartburn and acid reflux.
Pantoprazole.age: Generally for adults. Follow the label.
Pantoprazole.precautions: Not for immediate relief. Seek advice if symptoms last beyond a couple of weeks. Long-term use needs supervision.
Pantoprazole.interactions: Can interact with certain HIV medicines, clopidogrel and methotrexate.
Pantoprazole.status: OTC in some markets, prescription in others.
Pantoprazole.warning: Persistent symptoms, vomiting or black stools need medical review.

Esomeprazole.uses: Treatment of frequent heartburn and acid reflux.
Esomeprazole.age: Generally for adults. Follow the label.
Esomeprazole.precautions: Not for immediate relief; long-term use should be supervised.
Esomeprazole.interactions: Can interact with clopidogrel, methotrexate and some HIV medicines.
Esomeprazole.status: OTC in some markets, prescription in others.
Esomeprazole.warning: Do not use beyond the label period without medical advice.

Sodium Alginate.uses: Relief of heartburn and acid reflux by forming a protective layer.
Sodium Alginate.age: Age limits vary. Follow the label.
Sodium Alginate.precautions: Contains sodium; use caution in low-salt diets, heart or kidney disease.
Sodium Alginate.interactions: Separate from some medicines by a couple of hours.
Sodium Alginate.warning: Seek advice if symptoms are frequent.

Digestive Enzymes.uses: Short-term relief of bloating or fullness after heavy meals.
Digestive Enzymes.age: Age limits vary. Follow the label.
Digestive Enzymes.precautions: Avoid with pork allergy if derived from pork; use caution with pancreatic disease unless supervised.
Digestive Enzymes.warning: Not a substitute for evaluating persistent digestive problems.

Magnesium Hydroxide.uses: Short-term relief of occasional constipation and acidity.
Magnesium Hydroxide.age: Age limits vary. Follow the label.
Magnesium Hydroxide.precautions: Use caution in kidney disease. Not for long-term use.
Magnesium Hydroxide.interactions: Can reduce absorption of some medicines such as certain antibiotics.
Magnesium Hydroxide.warning: Do not use daily for long periods.

Senna.age: Age limits vary. Follow the label.
Senna.precautions: Avoid with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting or suspected blockage. Not for long-term use.
Senna.sideEffects: Cramps, diarrhea, electrolyte loss with overuse.
Senna.interactions: Overuse may worsen effects of some heart or diuretic medicines.
Senna.food: Often taken at bedtime; works in about 6 to 12 hours.
Senna.warning: Do not use for more than a week without advice.

Polyethylene Glycol (PEG).uses: Relief of constipation by softening stools.
Polyethylene Glycol (PEG).age: Age limits vary. Follow the label.
Polyethylene Glycol (PEG).precautions: Mix with the recommended amount of water. Stop if diarrhea develops.
Polyethylene Glycol (PEG).interactions: May reduce absorption of some medicines if taken at the same time.

Glycerin Suppository.age: Child and adult versions exist. Follow the label.
Glycerin Suppository.precautions: Do not use with rectal bleeding or severe pain.

Racecadotril.uses: Short-term treatment of acute watery diarrhea alongside oral rehydration.
Racecadotril.age: Age limits apply. Follow the label or medical advice.
Racecadotril.precautions: Not for bloody diarrhea or diarrhea with high fever. Does not replace ORS.
Racecadotril.status: OTC or prescription depending on the country.
Racecadotril.warning: Seek care for blood in stools, high fever or dehydration.

Bismuth Subsalicylate.uses: Relief of mild diarrhea, indigestion, nausea and upset stomach.
Bismuth Subsalicylate.age: Avoid in children and teens recovering from viral illness. Follow the label.
Bismuth Subsalicylate.precautions: Contains salicylate; avoid with aspirin allergy, bleeding disorders or ulcers.
Bismuth Subsalicylate.sideEffects: Harmless black stools or tongue discoloration; constipation.
Bismuth Subsalicylate.interactions: Interacts with aspirin, blood thinners and some antibiotics.
Bismuth Subsalicylate.warning: Do not use with fever and bloody stools; seek care.

Dicyclomine.uses: Relief of stomach and intestinal cramps and IBS spasms.
Dicyclomine.age: Age limits apply. Follow the label.
Dicyclomine.precautions: Avoid with glaucoma, urinary retention or severe constipation.
Dicyclomine.sideEffects: Dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, drowsiness.
Dicyclomine.interactions: Adds to other anticholinergic medicines such as antihistamines.
Dicyclomine.status: OTC or prescription depending on the country.
Dicyclomine.warning: Avoid driving if it makes you dizzy.

Mebeverine.uses: Relief of cramping and abdominal pain from irritable bowel syndrome.
Mebeverine.age: Generally for adults and older children. Follow the label.
Mebeverine.precautions: Seek advice if symptoms are new or severe.
Mebeverine.status: OTC or prescription depending on the country.
Mebeverine.warning: Persistent or worsening symptoms need medical review.

Peppermint Oil Capsule.uses: Relief of bloating and abdominal cramps in IBS.
Peppermint Oil Capsule.precautions: Swallow whole. May worsen heartburn or reflux.
Peppermint Oil Capsule.interactions: May affect some medicines metabolized by the liver.
Peppermint Oil Capsule.status: Supplement or OTC depending on the market.
Peppermint Oil Capsule.warning: Avoid with severe reflux or gallstones unless advised.

Ginger Supplement.uses: Relief of mild nausea and motion sickness.
Ginger Supplement.precautions: Use caution with blood thinners, gallstones or before surgery.
Ginger Supplement.interactions: May enhance the effect of blood thinners.
Ginger Supplement.warning: Not a substitute for care if vomiting persists.

Meclizine.purpose: Antihistamine for vertigo and motion sickness
Meclizine.uses: Prevention of motion sickness and relief of vertigo-related nausea.
Meclizine.age: Age limits vary. Follow the label.
Meclizine.precautions: Causes drowsiness. Avoid with glaucoma, enlarged prostate or asthma, and when driving.
Meclizine.interactions: Adds to alcohol and other sedatives.
Meclizine.status: OTC in some markets, prescription in others.
Meclizine.warning: Sudden dizziness with weakness, speech trouble or chest pain needs emergency care.

Mebendazole.uses: Treatment of common intestinal worm infections.
Mebendazole.age: Age limits apply. Follow the label.
Mebendazole.precautions: Avoid in the first trimester of pregnancy. Treat household contacts if advised.
Mebendazole.interactions: Cimetidine and some other medicines can alter levels.
Mebendazole.status: OTC or prescription depending on the country.
Mebendazole.warning: Complete the course; seek advice if symptoms persist.

Benzyl Benzoate.uses: Treatment of scabies by applying to the whole body below the neck.
Benzyl Benzoate.age: Needs dilution or special use in children. Follow medical guidance.
Benzyl Benzoate.precautions: Avoid eyes and mucous membranes. Treat all close contacts and wash bedding.
Benzyl Benzoate.interactions: No significant interactions with topical use.
Benzyl Benzoate.status: OTC in some markets, prescription in others.
Benzyl Benzoate.warning: Do not use on broken skin; follow the full schedule.

Dimeticone Lotion.uses: Treatment of head lice by coating and suffocating lice.
Dimeticone Lotion.age: Age limits apply; follow the label.
Dimeticone Lotion.precautions: Keep away from eyes. Use a fine-toothed comb afterwards and repeat as directed.
Dimeticone Lotion.warning: Flammable in some forms; avoid heat during use.

Miconazole.uses: Treatment of athlete's foot, ringworm, jock itch and yeast infections.
Miconazole.age: Age limits vary. Follow the label.
Miconazole.precautions: Use only on intended areas; complete the full course even if symptoms improve.
Miconazole.interactions: Can increase the effect of warfarin even with topical use.
Miconazole.warning: Seek advice if no improvement or for recurrent infections.

Zinc Pyrithione Shampoo.uses: Control of dandruff and flaky scalp.
Zinc Pyrithione Shampoo.age: Age limits vary. Follow the label.
Zinc Pyrithione Shampoo.precautions: Avoid eyes; stop if irritation develops.
Zinc Pyrithione Shampoo.warning: Seek advice if the scalp is very red, painful or oozing.

Selenium Sulfide Shampoo.uses: Treatment of dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis.
Selenium Sulfide Shampoo.age: Age limits vary. Follow the label.
Selenium Sulfide Shampoo.precautions: Rinse well; avoid eyes. May discolor hair or jewelry.
Selenium Sulfide Shampoo.warning: Do not use on broken or inflamed skin.

Coal Tar Preparation.uses: Relief of scaling and itching in psoriasis, seborrheic dermatitis and dandruff.
Coal Tar Preparation.age: Not for young children unless advised.
Coal Tar Preparation.precautions: Can stain, cause photosensitivity and smell strongly. Avoid broken skin and eyes.
Coal Tar Preparation.warning: Avoid prolonged sun exposure after use.

Adapalene.uses: Treatment of mild to moderate acne.
Adapalene.age: Generally for adolescents and adults. Follow the label.
Adapalene.precautions: Avoid in pregnancy. Use sunscreen; apply to dry skin at night. Avoid broken skin and eyes.
Adapalene.sideEffects: Dryness, redness, peeling, stinging, especially early on.
Adapalene.interactions: Avoid combining with other irritating products unless advised.
Adapalene.warning: Results take weeks; do not overuse.

Antibiotic Ointment (Neomycin/Bacitracin.uses: Help prevent infection in minor cuts, scrapes and burns.
Antibiotic Ointment (Neomycin/Bacitracin.precautions: Use only on small, minor wounds for a short time. Neomycin can cause contact allergy.
Antibiotic Ointment (Neomycin/Bacitracin.warning: Seek care for deep, dirty or spreading infections.

Petroleum Jelly.uses: Protecting dry, chapped, irritated or healing skin.
Petroleum Jelly.age: Safe for all ages when used on skin.
Petroleum Jelly.precautions: Do not use on infected wounds or deep burns unless advised.
Petroleum Jelly.sideEffects: Rarely clogs pores or causes irritation.
Petroleum Jelly.warning: Do not apply to very hot or freshly burned skin.

Urea Cream.uses: Relief of dry, rough or scaly skin, eczema and psoriasis.
Urea Cream.age: Age limits vary. Follow the label.
Urea Cream.precautions: Avoid broken or inflamed skin and eyes at higher strengths.
Urea Cream.warning: Higher strengths may need professional guidance.

Colloidal Oatmeal Lotion.uses: Relief of itching and dryness in eczema, rashes and sensitive skin.
Colloidal Oatmeal Lotion.precautions: Patch test if prone to allergies.
Colloidal Oatmeal Lotion.warning: Seek advice for infected or oozing rashes.

Zinc Oxide Ointment.uses: Protection of irritated skin, minor rashes and soothing of hemorrhoids.
Zinc Oxide Ointment.precautions: Do not use on deep or infected wounds.
Zinc Oxide Ointment.warning: Seek advice for persistent rash or bleeding.

Prickly Heat Powder.uses: Relief of heat rash and itching in hot weather.
Prickly Heat Powder.age: Avoid use on infants unless the label allows.
Prickly Heat Powder.precautions: Avoid inhaling; do not use on broken skin or near eyes.

Olive / Mineral Oil Ear Drops.precautions: Do not use with ear pain, discharge or a perforated eardrum.
Olive / Mineral Oil Ear Drops.warning: Do not insert objects into the ear.

Carboxymethylcellulose Eye Drops.uses: Relief of dry, irritated or tired eyes.
Carboxymethylcellulose Eye Drops.age: Safe for most ages; follow the label.
Carboxymethylcellulose Eye Drops.precautions: Avoid touching the dropper to the eye. Remove contact lenses unless drops are lens-safe.
Carboxymethylcellulose Eye Drops.interactions: Wait several minutes between different eye drops.
Carboxymethylcellulose Eye Drops.warning: Seek care for eye pain, vision change or discharge.

Clove Oil.uses: Temporary soothing of tooth and gum pain.
Clove Oil.precautions: Dilute and apply to the tooth only; avoid swallowing and prolonged use.
Clove Oil.interactions: May enhance the effect of blood thinners if swallowed.
Clove Oil.status: Available OTC or as a traditional remedy.
Clove Oil.warning: Does not treat the cause; see a dentist.

Vitamin C Supplement.uses: Supports immune function and iron absorption; used for vitamin C deficiency.
Vitamin C Supplement.age: Dose depends on age. Follow the label.
Vitamin C Supplement.precautions: High doses can upset the stomach; caution with kidney stones or iron overload.
Vitamin C Supplement.sideEffects: Stomach upset, diarrhea at high doses.
Vitamin C Supplement.warning: Does not prevent or cure colds in most people.

Vitamin B-Complex.ingredient: Thiamine, riboflavin, niacin, B6, B12 and others
Vitamin B-Complex.uses: Supports energy metabolism and may help with deficiency-related fatigue or mouth sores.
Vitamin B-Complex.age: Dose depends on age. Follow the label.
Vitamin B-Complex.interactions: Certain medicines may interact with specific B vitamins.
Vitamin B-Complex.warning: Not a replacement for a balanced diet.

Magnesium Supplement.uses: Used for low magnesium, muscle cramps and PMS discomfort.
Magnesium Supplement.age: Dose depends on age. Follow the label.
Magnesium Supplement.precautions: Use caution in kidney disease. Excess can cause diarrhea.
Magnesium Supplement.interactions: Can reduce absorption of some antibiotics and bisphosphonates.

Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine).uses: Used for B6 deficiency and sometimes for PMS or pregnancy-related nausea under advice.
Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine).age: Dose depends on age. Follow the label.
Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine).precautions: Long-term high doses can cause nerve damage.
Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine).sideEffects: Nausea, headache, tingling at high doses.
Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine).interactions: May reduce the effect of levodopa and some seizure medicines.

Disodium Hydrogen Citrate.uses: Eases burning during urination in minor urinary discomfort.
Disodium Hydrogen Citrate.age: Age limits apply. Follow the label.
Disodium Hydrogen Citrate.precautions: Does not treat infection. Avoid in kidney disease, heart failure or low-salt diets.
Disodium Hydrogen Citrate.interactions: May affect absorption of some medicines.
Disodium Hydrogen Citrate.status: OTC in India and some markets.
Disodium Hydrogen Citrate.warning: UTI usually needs a doctor and urine test; seek care if fever, back pain or blood in urine.

Metformin.uses: Used in type 2 diabetes to help control blood glucose.
Metformin.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Metformin.precautions: Kidney and liver function should be monitored; may need to be paused before some scans or surgery.
Metformin.sideEffects: Nausea, diarrhea, stomach upset, metallic taste.
Metformin.interactions: Alcohol and some contrast dyes can increase risk of serious side effects.
Metformin.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Metformin.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Glimepiride.uses: Used in type 2 diabetes to increase insulin release.
Glimepiride.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Glimepiride.precautions: Can cause low blood sugar; know the signs and carry fast-acting sugar.
Glimepiride.sideEffects: Low blood sugar, weight gain, dizziness.
Glimepiride.interactions: Other diabetes medicines and alcohol can increase the risk of low blood sugar.
Glimepiride.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Glimepiride.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Insulin.uses: Replaces or supplements the body's insulin in diabetes.
Insulin.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Insulin.precautions: Type, dose and timing are individual; blood sugar monitoring is important.
Insulin.sideEffects: Low blood sugar, injection-site reactions, weight gain.
Insulin.interactions: Many medicines and alcohol can change blood sugar response.
Insulin.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Insulin.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Amlodipine.uses: Used for high blood pressure and certain types of chest pain.
Amlodipine.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Amlodipine.precautions: Blood pressure should be monitored regularly.
Amlodipine.interactions: Grapefruit and some medicines may change its effect.
Amlodipine.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Amlodipine.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Telmisartan.uses: Used for high blood pressure and heart protection.
Telmisartan.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Telmisartan.precautions: Not for use in pregnancy; kidney function and potassium may need monitoring.
Telmisartan.interactions: NSAIDs, potassium supplements and some diuretics may interact.
Telmisartan.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Telmisartan.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Losartan.uses: Used for high blood pressure and kidney protection in some conditions.
Losartan.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Losartan.precautions: Not for use in pregnancy; kidney function and potassium may need monitoring.
Losartan.interactions: NSAIDs and potassium supplements may interact.
Losartan.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Losartan.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Atorvastatin.uses: Used to lower LDL cholesterol and reduce heart disease risk.
Atorvastatin.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Atorvastatin.precautions: Liver tests may be needed; report unexplained muscle pain.
Atorvastatin.interactions: Grapefruit juice in large amounts and some antibiotics may interact.
Atorvastatin.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Atorvastatin.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Rosuvastatin.uses: Used to lower LDL cholesterol and reduce heart disease risk.
Rosuvastatin.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Rosuvastatin.precautions: Report unexplained muscle pain or weakness; avoid in pregnancy.
Rosuvastatin.interactions: Some antacids, blood thinners and other medicines may interact.
Rosuvastatin.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Rosuvastatin.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Levothyroxine.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Levothyroxine.precautions: Regular thyroid blood tests are needed to set the correct amount.
Levothyroxine.sideEffects: Palpitations, anxiety or sleep trouble if the amount is too high.
Levothyroxine.interactions: Calcium, iron and antacids can reduce absorption; keep a gap.
Levothyroxine.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Levothyroxine.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Carbimazole.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Carbimazole.precautions: Report sore throat or fever promptly; blood tests are needed.
Carbimazole.sideEffects: Rash, nausea, joint pain; rarely low white blood cells.
Carbimazole.interactions: Tell your doctor about all medicines you take.
Carbimazole.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Carbimazole.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Orlistat.uses: Used with a reduced-calorie diet in some people with obesity.
Orlistat.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Orlistat.precautions: Works best with a low-fat diet; a multivitamin may be advised.
Orlistat.interactions: May reduce absorption of fat-soluble vitamins and some medicines.
Orlistat.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Orlistat.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Norethisterone.uses: Used by doctors for some menstrual problems.
Norethisterone.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Norethisterone.precautions: Needs medical evaluation of the cause first; not a contraceptive unless prescribed as one.
Norethisterone.interactions: Some epilepsy and TB medicines may interact.
Norethisterone.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Norethisterone.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Ashwagandha Supplement.uses: Traditionally used for stress and general wellbeing.
Ashwagandha Supplement.age: Follow the exact product label; ask a pharmacist for children.
Ashwagandha Supplement.precautions: Avoid in pregnancy; use caution with thyroid conditions and sedatives.
Ashwagandha Supplement.interactions: May add to the effect of sedatives and thyroid medicines.
Ashwagandha Supplement.status: Available OTC or as a supplement in many markets.
Ashwagandha Supplement.warning: Do not exceed the label directions. See a doctor if symptoms persist or worsen.

Escitalopram.uses: Used by doctors for anxiety and depression.
Escitalopram.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Escitalopram.precautions: Do not stop suddenly; benefits take weeks and mood should be monitored.
Escitalopram.sideEffects: Nausea, sleep changes, sexual side effects.
Escitalopram.interactions: Other serotonergic medicines, blood thinners and NSAIDs may interact.
Escitalopram.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Escitalopram.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Budesonide Inhaler.uses: Used daily to reduce airway inflammation in asthma.
Budesonide Inhaler.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Budesonide Inhaler.precautions: Rinse the mouth after each use to reduce thrush.
Budesonide Inhaler.interactions: Some antifungals can raise its levels.
Budesonide Inhaler.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Budesonide Inhaler.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Montelukast.uses: Used for asthma prevention and some allergic rhinitis.
Montelukast.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Montelukast.precautions: Report mood or sleep changes promptly.
Montelukast.interactions: Some seizure medicines may change its effect.
Montelukast.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Montelukast.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Nitrofurantoin.uses: Used for uncomplicated urinary tract infections.
Nitrofurantoin.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Nitrofurantoin.precautions: Needs a doctor's diagnosis; avoid with poor kidney function.
Nitrofurantoin.interactions: Antacids with magnesium may reduce absorption.
Nitrofurantoin.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Nitrofurantoin.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Cranberry Supplement.uses: Sometimes used to help reduce recurrent UTIs; not a treatment for an active infection.
Cranberry Supplement.age: Follow the exact product label; ask a pharmacist for children.
Cranberry Supplement.precautions: See a doctor for burning urination, fever or back pain.
Cranberry Supplement.status: Available OTC or as a supplement in many markets.
Cranberry Supplement.warning: Do not exceed the label directions. See a doctor if symptoms persist or worsen.

Electrolyte Powder.uses: Replaces fluids and salts lost through sweat, heat, vomiting or diarrhea.
Electrolyte Powder.age: Follow the exact product label; ask a pharmacist for children.
Electrolyte Powder.precautions: Mix exactly as directed; seek care for severe dehydration.
Electrolyte Powder.interactions: Check with a doctor if on a low-salt diet or with kidney disease.
Electrolyte Powder.status: Available OTC or as a supplement in many markets.
Electrolyte Powder.warning: Do not exceed the label directions. See a doctor if symptoms persist or worsen.

Wart Freeze Spray.uses: Freezes common and plantar warts at home.
Wart Freeze Spray.age: Follow the exact product label; ask a pharmacist for children.
Wart Freeze Spray.precautions: Do not use on the face, genitals or moles; avoid healthy skin.
Wart Freeze Spray.status: Available OTC or as a supplement in many markets.
Wart Freeze Spray.warning: Do not exceed the label directions. See a doctor if symptoms persist or worsen.

Colchicine.uses: Used to treat or prevent gout attacks.
Colchicine.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Colchicine.precautions: Dose must be kept low in kidney or liver disease.
Colchicine.interactions: Some antibiotics and statins increase toxicity risk.
Colchicine.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Colchicine.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Allopurinol.uses: Used long term to prevent gout attacks.
Allopurinol.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Allopurinol.precautions: Stop and seek care if a skin rash develops; start under medical advice.
Allopurinol.interactions: Some immune medicines and antibiotics may interact.
Allopurinol.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Allopurinol.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Biotin Supplement.uses: Often taken for hair and nail support when intake is low.
Biotin Supplement.age: Follow the exact product label; ask a pharmacist for children.
Biotin Supplement.precautions: Can interfere with some blood test results; tell the lab.
Biotin Supplement.interactions: May affect thyroid and heart blood tests.
Biotin Supplement.status: Available OTC or as a supplement in many markets.
Biotin Supplement.warning: Do not exceed the label directions. See a doctor if symptoms persist or worsen.

Tamsulosin.uses: Used by doctors to relax the urinary tract, for enlarged prostate symptoms and to help pass some kidney stones.
Tamsulosin.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Tamsulosin.precautions: May cause dizziness on standing; tell your eye surgeon before cataract surgery.
Tamsulosin.interactions: Other blood pressure medicines can add to the dizziness.
Tamsulosin.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Tamsulosin.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Alendronate.uses: Used for osteoporosis to slow bone loss.
Alendronate.age: Use in children and older adults depends on the condition and the doctor's assessment.
Alendronate.precautions: Take with a full glass of water and stay upright for 30 minutes; dental checks are advised.
Alendronate.sideEffects: Heartburn, stomach pain, bone or muscle ache.
Alendronate.interactions: Calcium, antacids and iron reduce absorption; keep a gap.
Alendronate.food: Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
Alendronate.warning: Start, change or stop only under a doctor's supervision. Never share prescription medicines.

Diosmin.uses: Used for symptoms of venous insufficiency such as heavy, tired legs and varicose veins.
Diosmin.age: Generally for adults; follow the label.
Diosmin.precautions: Swelling, skin changes or leg pain should be checked by a doctor.
Diosmin.interactions: Tell a pharmacist about other medicines.
Diosmin.food: Usually taken with meals; follow the label.
Diosmin.status: OTC or prescription depending on the country.
Diosmin.warning: See a doctor urgently for a painful, swollen, red leg.

Zinc Sulfate.uses: Reduces duration and severity of acute diarrhoea in children when given with ORS.
Zinc Sulfate.age: Age-specific dosing for children; follow national diarrhoea management guidelines.
Zinc Sulfate.precautions: Do not exceed recommended dose. Not a substitute for ORS and medical care.
Zinc Sulfate.sideEffects: Metallic taste, mild nausea or vomiting possible.
Zinc Sulfate.interactions: May reduce absorption of some antibiotics if taken together.
Zinc Sulfate.food: Can be given with or without food; follow product directions.

Mupirocin.uses: Used for impetigo and other superficial bacterial skin infections.
Mupirocin.age: Suitable for children and adults as directed by a clinician.
Mupirocin.precautions: For external use only. Avoid eyes. Prolonged use may lead to resistance.

Fusidic Acid Cream.uses: Treats bacterial skin infections including some cases of impetigo.
Fusidic Acid Cream.age: Can be used in children under medical advice.
Fusidic Acid Cream.precautions: External use only. Do not use on large areas for prolonged periods.

Hydrochlorothiazide.age: Common in older adults; watch electrolytes.
Hydrochlorothiazide.precautions: Can lower potassium and sodium. Photosensitivity possible.
Hydrochlorothiazide.sideEffects: Electrolyte imbalance, increased uric acid, dizziness.

Ciprofloxacin.uses: Certain bacterial infections including some UTIs (when indicated).
Ciprofloxacin.age: Generally avoided in children and used cautiously in older adults.
Ciprofloxacin.precautions: Tendon risk, especially in elderly. Photosensitivity. Avoid dairy around dose.
Ciprofloxacin.sideEffects: GI upset, dizziness, rare tendon rupture or CNS effects.
Ciprofloxacin.interactions: Many; including antacids, iron, warfarin, theophylline.

Doxylamine + Pyridoxine.uses: First-line pharmacologic option for morning sickness when lifestyle measures are insufficient.
Doxylamine + Pyridoxine.age: Used in pregnancy under medical advice.
Doxylamine + Pyridoxine.precautions: May cause drowsiness. Do not drive until response is known.

Ginger.uses: May help mild nausea of pregnancy and motion-related nausea.
Ginger.age: Commonly used; discuss dose in pregnancy with a clinician.
Ginger.precautions: High doses may have blood-thinning effects. Quality varies.
Ginger.sideEffects: Heartburn or mild stomach upset possible.
Ginger.food: Taken with food or as tea.

Iron + Folic Acid.purpose: Prevention and treatment of anaemia in pregnancy
Iron + Folic Acid.uses: Standard antenatal supplementation to prevent iron-deficiency anaemia and neural-tube defects.
Iron + Folic Acid.age: Routine in pregnancy; dose as per national guidelines.
Iron + Folic Acid.precautions: Constipation and dark stools common. Keep away from children.
Iron + Folic Acid.food: Best on empty stomach if tolerated; otherwise with food.

Ranitidine.uses: Previously used for heartburn; availability now limited in many countries due to regulatory actions.
Ranitidine.age: Check current local availability and alternatives.
Ranitidine.precautions: Many markets have withdrawn or restricted ranitidine. Prefer current approved options.
Ranitidine.interactions: May affect absorption of some drugs.
Ranitidine.status: Restricted / withdrawn in many places — check local guidance

Fipronil Spot-on.uses: Kills fleas and ticks on dogs and cats when applied as directed.
Fipronil Spot-on.age: Age and weight specific products for pets; never use dog products on cats.
Fipronil Spot-on.precautions: For animal use only. Keep away from children and other pets until dry. Do not use on broken skin.
Fipronil Spot-on.sideEffects: Local irritation, rare neurological signs if licked excessively.
Fipronil Spot-on.interactions: Follow product label; avoid combining with other insecticides without advice.

Ivermectin.uses: In veterinary medicine: heartworm prevention, certain mites and worms. Human formulations are different products.
Ivermectin.age: Strictly follow species and weight dosing. Never use large-animal formulations on pets or humans.
Ivermectin.precautions: Species-specific toxicity (especially collies and some breeds). Veterinary guidance essential.
Ivermectin.sideEffects: In animals: neurological signs if overdosed or sensitive breeds.

Doxycycline (Vet).uses: Bacterial infections in dogs and cats including some respiratory and tick-borne diseases.
Doxycycline (Vet).age: Dose by weight under veterinary direction. Avoid in very young animals when teeth are forming.
Doxycycline (Vet).precautions: Give with food to reduce oesophageal irritation. Complete the course.
Doxycycline (Vet).sideEffects: GI upset, photosensitivity, enamel effects in young animals.

Lysine.uses: Often used as supportive care for feline herpesvirus-related upper respiratory signs.
Lysine.precautions: Not a cure; supportive only. Veterinary advice recommended.
Lysine.sideEffects: Usually well tolerated; high doses may cause GI upset.

Metronidazole (Vet).uses: Certain bacterial and protozoal causes of diarrhoea in dogs and cats.
Metronidazole (Vet).precautions: Neurological toxicity possible at high doses or prolonged use. Bitter taste.
Metronidazole (Vet).interactions: Alcohol-like reactions possible; other drugs as per vet.

Probiotic (Vet).uses: Adjunct during and after diarrhoea or antibiotic courses in dogs and cats.
Probiotic (Vet).precautions: Supportive only; not a substitute for diagnosis and treatment of serious disease.

Pyrantel Pamoate (Vet).uses: Treats roundworms and hookworms in dogs and cats.
Pyrantel Pamoate (Vet).age: Weight and age appropriate; common in puppy/kitten protocols.
Pyrantel Pamoate (Vet).precautions: Follow label; some products are species specific.
Pyrantel Pamoate (Vet).interactions: Generally safe with other common dewormers when sequenced properly.

Fenbendazole.uses: Treats various intestinal worms and some other parasites in dogs, cats and other species.
Fenbendazole.age: Dose by weight for the specific species under veterinary guidance.
Fenbendazole.precautions: Complete the recommended course length. Safe in many species when dosed correctly.
Fenbendazole.interactions: Minimal clinically important interactions at standard doses.

Glucosamine.uses: Popular supportive option for osteoarthritis symptoms in older adults and also used in veterinary joint products.
Glucosamine.age: Adults and older pets; evidence is mixed but widely used.
Glucosamine.precautions: Not a substitute for prescribed pain relief or disease-modifying treatment.
Glucosamine.interactions: Theoretical effect on blood sugar and warfarin; monitor if relevant.

Dexamethasone.uses: Reduces airway inflammation in croup and other selected inflammatory conditions under medical care.
Dexamethasone.age: Dose is weight-based in children; given as a short course for croup.
Dexamethasone.precautions: Short courses are usually well tolerated; prolonged use needs specialist supervision.
Dexamethasone.sideEffects: Increased appetite, mood change, raised blood sugar with longer use.
Dexamethasone.interactions: NSAIDs, some antifungals and live vaccines.
Dexamethasone.food: Can be taken with food to reduce stomach upset.

Amoxicillin.uses: Common bacterial infections including many cases of childhood ear infection when indicated.
Amoxicillin.age: Widely used in children with age and weight-based dosing.
Amoxicillin.precautions: Allergy to penicillins is a contraindication. Complete the course.
Amoxicillin.food: Can be taken with or without food.

Polyethylene Glycol.uses: Chronic constipation in children and adults when fibre and fluids are insufficient.
Polyethylene Glycol.age: Paediatric formulations and doses available; follow product or clinician advice.
Polyethylene Glycol.precautions: Ensure adequate fluid intake. Not for sudden severe abdominal pain until assessed.
Polyethylene Glycol.sideEffects: Bloating, flatulence, loose stools if dose too high.
Polyethylene Glycol.interactions: May affect absorption of other oral medicines if taken at the same time.
Polyethylene Glycol.food: Mixed with water; can be flavoured.

Emollient Cream.purpose: Skin moisturiser for dry and eczematous skin
Emollient Cream.uses: Regular application to reduce dryness and flare frequency in atopic eczema.
Emollient Cream.age: Safe for infants and children when fragrance-free products are chosen.
Emollient Cream.precautions: Apply liberally and often. Avoid products with known irritants.
Emollient Cream.sideEffects: Rarely local irritation; choose simple formulations.

Adapalene Gel.uses: Mild to moderate acne, especially comedonal acne in adolescents and adults.
Adapalene Gel.age: Typically from early adolescence; follow product age limits.
Adapalene Gel.precautions: Use sunscreen; may cause dryness and irritation initially. Avoid eyes and lips.
Adapalene Gel.sideEffects: Redness, peeling, dryness, especially in first weeks.
Adapalene Gel.interactions: Other irritating topicals may increase irritation.

Ondansetron.uses: Reduces vomiting in gastroenteritis and other causes when prescribed.
