Ondansetron.age: Used in children under medical guidance for selected indications.
Ondansetron.precautions: Can prolong QT interval; avoid in known long QT. Not for routine mild nausea.
Ondansetron.food: Can be taken with or without food.

Sitagliptin.uses: Improves blood glucose control, often added to metformin.
Sitagliptin.age: Used in older adults; dose adjust in renal impairment.
Sitagliptin.precautions: Monitor kidney function. Rare risk of pancreatitis.
Sitagliptin.sideEffects: Nasopharyngitis, headache; rare severe joint pain.

Gliclazide.uses: Stimulates insulin release in type 2 diabetes.
Gliclazide.age: Used in older adults with caution because of hypoglycaemia risk.
Gliclazide.precautions: Hypoglycaemia risk rises with missed meals, alcohol or renal impairment.
Gliclazide.sideEffects: Low blood sugar, weight gain, GI upset.
Gliclazide.interactions: Many drugs affect glucose control or potentiate hypoglycaemia.

Furosemide.uses: Reduces fluid overload in heart failure and other oedematous states.
Furosemide.age: Common in older adults; monitor electrolytes and kidney function.
Furosemide.precautions: Can cause dehydration and low potassium. Take in the morning.

Spironolactone.uses: Heart failure, resistant hypertension, some cases of oedema.
Spironolactone.age: Used in older adults; watch potassium closely.
Spironolactone.precautions: Hyperkalaemia risk, especially with ACE inhibitors or ARBs and reduced kidney function.
Spironolactone.sideEffects: Raised potassium, breast tenderness, menstrual changes.
Spironolactone.interactions: Potassium supplements, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, trimethoprim.

Bisoprolol.uses: Heart failure, hypertension, angina; rate control.
Bisoprolol.age: Widely used in older adults with careful titration.
Bisoprolol.precautions: Do not stop suddenly. Caution in asthma and severe bradycardia.
Bisoprolol.sideEffects: Tiredness, cold extremities, slow heart rate, dizziness.
Bisoprolol.interactions: Other rate-slowing drugs, some calcium channel blockers.
Bisoprolol.food: Consistent timing; with or without food.

Finasteride.uses: Reduces prostate size and improves lower urinary tract symptoms over months.
Finasteride.age: Older men; not for use in women of childbearing potential.
Finasteride.precautions: Women who are or may become pregnant should not handle crushed tablets.
Finasteride.sideEffects: Reduced libido, erectile dysfunction, breast tenderness (usually uncommon).

Calcium + Vitamin D.uses: Prevention and treatment of calcium and vitamin D deficiency; osteoporosis support.
Calcium + Vitamin D.age: Common in older adults and in pregnancy.
Calcium + Vitamin D.precautions: Do not exceed recommended dose. Check total calcium intake from other sources.
Calcium + Vitamin D.sideEffects: Constipation, nausea, rare hypercalcaemia at high doses.
Calcium + Vitamin D.interactions: Reduces absorption of some antibiotics and thyroid hormone if taken together.
Calcium + Vitamin D.food: Often with meals; space from other interacting medicines.

Levodopa + Carbidopa.uses: Mainstay treatment for motor symptoms of Parkinson disease.
Levodopa + Carbidopa.precautions: Doses are individualised. Protein may affect absorption. Do not stop abruptly.
Levodopa + Carbidopa.sideEffects: Nausea, dizziness, dyskinesias, hallucinations at higher doses.
Levodopa + Carbidopa.food: Consistent relation to meals as advised.

Pramipexole.uses: Parkinson disease and restless legs syndrome.
Pramipexole.age: Older adults; start low and go slow.
Pramipexole.precautions: Sleep attacks, impulse control behaviours, hallucinations possible.

Artificial Tears.uses: Relieves dryness and irritation of the eyes.
Artificial Tears.age: Suitable for older adults; preservative-free preferred for frequent use.
Artificial Tears.precautions: Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye. Discard according to label.
Artificial Tears.interactions: Wait before using other eye drops.

Carboxymethylcellulose Drops.precautions: Preservative-free units preferred for frequent dosing.
Carboxymethylcellulose Drops.interactions: Space from other topical ocular medicines.

Topical NSAID Gel.uses: Local joint and soft-tissue pain with lower systemic exposure than oral NSAIDs.
Topical NSAID Gel.age: Useful option in older adults to reduce systemic risk.
Topical NSAID Gel.precautions: Do not use on broken skin. Still use caution if high cardiovascular or renal risk.
Topical NSAID Gel.sideEffects: Local skin irritation, photosensitivity with some agents.
Topical NSAID Gel.interactions: Systemic NSAID risk is lower but not zero with large areas.

Tramadol.uses: Moderate pain when other options are insufficient.
Tramadol.age: Use cautiously in older adults; start low.
Tramadol.precautions: Seizure risk, serotonin syndrome with certain antidepressants, dependence potential.
Tramadol.interactions: SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs, other CNS depressants.

Sertraline.uses: Depression, anxiety disorders; often preferred in older adults among SSRIs.
Sertraline.age: Used across adult ages including older adults; start low.
Sertraline.precautions: Suicidality monitoring early in treatment. Hyponatraemia risk in elderly.
Sertraline.sideEffects: Nausea, sleep change, sexual dysfunction, diarrhoea.
Sertraline.interactions: MAOIs, other serotonergic drugs, some anticoagulants.

Mirtazapine.uses: Depression, especially when sleep or appetite is reduced.
Mirtazapine.age: Often chosen in older adults for sedative and appetite effects.
Mirtazapine.precautions: Sedation, weight gain, rare blood dyscrasias.

Vitamin D3.uses: Correction and prevention of vitamin D deficiency; supports bone and muscle health.
Vitamin D3.age: Common in older adults and in pregnancy when indicated.
Vitamin D3.precautions: High doses need monitoring of calcium. Do not exceed recommended amounts without advice.
Vitamin D3.sideEffects: Rare at standard doses; high doses can cause hypercalcaemia.
Vitamin D3.food: Fat-soluble; often with a meal containing fat.

Zinc Oxide Paste.uses: Protects peri-ulcer skin and soothes irritated areas as part of leg ulcer care.
Zinc Oxide Paste.precautions: For external use. Clean skin before application as advised.

Compression advice support.ingredient: Not a drug – compression therapy support
Compression advice support.purpose: Supportive care note for venous leg ulcers
Compression advice support.uses: Compression is first-line for venous leg ulcers when arterial supply is adequate; medicines alone are not enough.
Compression advice support.precautions: Must exclude significant arterial disease before high compression. Specialist assessment needed.

Cephalexin.uses: Urinary and other bacterial infections; often considered in pregnancy when indicated.
Cephalexin.age: Adults including pregnant women when benefits outweigh risks.
Cephalexin.precautions: Allergy to cephalosporins or severe penicillin allergy is a concern.

Labetalol.uses: Blood pressure control in pregnancy-related hypertension when treatment is needed.
Labetalol.age: Used in pregnancy under specialist or obstetric guidance.
Labetalol.precautions: Monitor mother and fetus. Caution in asthma.

Nifedipine.uses: Hypertension in pregnancy and preterm labour tocolysis in selected protocols.
Nifedipine.precautions: Avoid immediate-release capsules for hypertension. Monitor blood pressure.
Nifedipine.interactions: Grapefruit juice, other antihypertensives, magnesium sulfate.
Nifedipine.food: Consistent relation to meals as per product.

Lidocaine Cream.uses: Temporary relief of haemorrhoid pain and itching.
Lidocaine Cream.age: Adults including in pregnancy for short-term local use as directed.
Lidocaine Cream.precautions: External use only. Do not exceed recommended amount or duration.

Ferrous Sulfate.uses: Treatment and prevention of iron-deficiency anaemia, including in pregnancy.
Ferrous Sulfate.age: Adults and pregnancy; paediatric forms exist for children.
Ferrous Sulfate.precautions: Keep away from children (overdose risk). Constipation and dark stools common.
Ferrous Sulfate.sideEffects: Nausea, constipation, black stools, abdominal discomfort.
Ferrous Sulfate.interactions: Tea, coffee, calcium and antacids reduce absorption; space doses.
Ferrous Sulfate.food: Best on empty stomach if tolerated; otherwise with food.

Oclacitinib.purpose: JAK inhibitor for allergic itch in dogs
Oclacitinib.uses: Controls pruritus associated with allergic dermatitis and atopic dermatitis in dogs.
Oclacitinib.age: Dogs of specified age and weight per label; not for cats.
Oclacitinib.precautions: Veterinary prescription only. Monitor for infections; not for use in dogs with serious infections.
Oclacitinib.sideEffects: Vomiting, diarrhoea, lethargy, possible increased infection risk.

Apoquel support.uses: Same class as oclacitinib products used for canine allergic dermatitis.

Antihistamine (Vet).uses: Sometimes used as adjunct for mild allergic itching; response is variable.
Antihistamine (Vet).age: Dose strictly by weight and species under veterinary guidance.
Antihistamine (Vet).precautions: Human products are not automatically safe for pets. Never guess the dose.
Antihistamine (Vet).sideEffects: Sedation, dry mouth, paradoxical excitement in some animals.

Prazosin (Vet).purpose: Alpha-blocker used in feline urinary issues
Prazosin (Vet).uses: Helps relax urethral smooth muscle in cats with lower urinary tract disease when prescribed.
Prazosin (Vet).precautions: Can lower blood pressure. Not a substitute for emergency care if the cat cannot urinate.
Prazosin (Vet).sideEffects: Lethargy, low blood pressure, GI upset.

Buprenorphine (Vet).uses: Pain relief in cats and dogs for selected conditions including urinary pain.
Buprenorphine (Vet).age: Species and weight specific under veterinary control.
Buprenorphine (Vet).precautions: Controlled drug in many regions. Strict dosing and monitoring.
Buprenorphine (Vet).sideEffects: Sedation, reduced appetite, rare respiratory depression.

Ear Cleaner (Vet).purpose: Ear hygiene for dogs and cats
Ear Cleaner (Vet).uses: Removes debris and prepares the ear before medicated drops when recommended.
Ear Cleaner (Vet).age: Species-appropriate products; avoid if the eardrum may be ruptured unless advised.
Ear Cleaner (Vet).precautions: Do not use if you suspect a ruptured tympanic membrane without veterinary advice.
Ear Cleaner (Vet).interactions: Follow sequence given by the vet with medicated drops.

Gentamicin + Betamethasone Ear Drops.uses: Bacterial otitis externa in dogs (and sometimes cats) when prescribed.
Gentamicin + Betamethasone Ear Drops.precautions: Confirm eardrum integrity. Complete the course. Not for viral or uncomplicated mite disease alone.
Gentamicin + Betamethasone Ear Drops.sideEffects: Local irritation; hearing risk if middle ear is exposed.

Cough suppressant (Vet).ingredient: Various (e.g. butorphanol, dextromethorphan in some regions – vet only)
Cough suppressant (Vet).uses: May reduce cough severity in kennel cough when specifically recommended.
Cough suppressant (Vet).precautions: Do not use human cough medicines without explicit veterinary instruction.
Cough suppressant (Vet).sideEffects: Sedation or GI upset depending on agent.

Insulin (Vet).uses: Mainstay of treatment for diabetes mellitus in dogs and cats.
Insulin (Vet).age: Lifelong management under veterinary supervision with home monitoring.
Insulin (Vet).precautions: Hypoglycaemia risk. Consistent feeding and injection timing essential. Never share human pens without guidance.
Insulin (Vet).sideEffects: Low blood sugar if mismatched with food or dose.
Insulin (Vet).interactions: Corticosteroids and some other drugs raise glucose needs.

Glipizide (Vet).purpose: Oral antidiabetic sometimes used in cats
Glipizide (Vet).uses: Selected cases of feline diabetes when insulin is not feasible and the cat still produces some insulin.
Glipizide (Vet).precautions: Less reliable than insulin; monitoring still required.

Carprofen.uses: Pain and inflammation in dogs with osteoarthritis and post-operative pain.
Carprofen.age: Dogs of appropriate age and health status; not for cats unless specifically authorised product.
Carprofen.precautions: Baseline blood tests often advised. Avoid in dehydrated, kidney or GI disease. Never combine with other NSAIDs or steroids without advice.
Carprofen.sideEffects: Vomiting, diarrhoea, reduced appetite, rare kidney or liver injury.
Carprofen.interactions: Other NSAIDs, corticosteroids, some cardiac and renal drugs.

Gabapentin (Vet).purpose: Neuropathic pain and anxiety support in animals
Gabapentin (Vet).uses: Chronic pain, osteoarthritis adjunct, and situational anxiety in dogs and cats.
Gabapentin (Vet).precautions: Sedation common. Dose carefully in kidney disease.

Prednisolone (Vet).uses: Allergic skin disease, inflammation and selected immune-mediated conditions in pets.
Prednisolone (Vet).age: Species and weight specific; taper as directed.
Prednisolone (Vet).precautions: Increases thirst, urination and appetite. Long-term use needs monitoring. Do not stop abruptly after prolonged courses.
